statement: Let n = len(coordinates). For 0 <= i < n let x_i = coordinates[i][0] and y_i = coordinates[i][1], interpreted as mathematical integers. For 0 <= i,j,k < n define D(i,j,k) = (x_j - x_i)*(y_k - y_i) - (y_j - y_i)*(x_k - x_i). Whenever the function returns a result r, r = true if and only if for every i,j,k with 0 <= i < j < k < n, D(i,j,k) = 0. When n = 2 this condition is vacuous and r must be true.
preconditions: 2 <= len(coordinates) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(coordinates), len(coordinates[i]) = 2, -10000 <= coordinates[i][0] <= 10000, and -10000 <= coordinates[i][1] <= 10000; for every i,j with 0 <= i < j < len(coordinates), not (coordinates[i][0] = coordinates[j][0] and coordinates[i][1] = coordinates[j][1]).
